clue.text: One found guilty on the wrong grounds

definitions.text: One found guilty on the wrong grounds

parts.words: One found guilty on the wrong grounds
parts.note: read 'on the wrong grounds' literally: someone caught standing on land where they have no right to be

explanation.surface: A court convicts someone on a faulty legal basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong grounds' looks like a legal phrase about a flawed verdict; it actually means somebody else's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters private land without permission is guilty of being on property they have no right to occupy.

indicators.note: something detained is held inside, so the nurse word holds the home word within it

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital ward
at home means in

explanation.surface: A nurse is held prisoner in her own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' is the British title for a senior ward nurse; the surface pictures a nurse kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something wicked or threatening harm, a close synonym of evil.

indicators.note: around says the reversed word wraps itself round the next piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled, on horseback or by vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reporter made a journey north and circled about.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom, so the travel word turns backwards before taking in the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper professional who prepares and oversees what journalists write, so is one kind of journalist.

clue.text: Unknown result of a French vote

parts.note: non is French for no, a vote against

explanation.surface: The outcome of a ballot in France is not yet declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, describing an author whose name is not known.

clue.text: Two lots of clothes worn in cars, eventually

parts.note: gear is clothing, as in sports gear
shifts are loose dresses, a second kind of clothing

explanation.surface: Two sets of outfits get put on inside motor vehicles over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' pretends to continue the clothes picture, but it means wearing down: the gear lever mechanism gets worn out in a car with use.
explanation.definitionFit: Gearshifts are the mechanisms for changing gear in a car, parts that wear out with long use.

parts.note: spelling here means casting spells, not putting letters in order

explanation.definitionFit: A magician or sorcerer works magic by uttering spells, so is literally an expert in spells.

clue.text: Island games organizers assemble for meal

parts.note: the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea
the IOC, International Olympic Committee, organizes the Olympic Games

explanation.surface: Organizers of island sports gather to eat together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' means coarse flour here, not a dinner; 'assemble for' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is cassava, a tropical root ground into a flour or meal used for tapioca and bread.

clue.text: Try out eastern source of purple dye

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Experiment with an oriental plant from which purple colouring comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try out' reads as one phrase meaning test, but 'out' is the anagram signal alone; 'eastern' then adds its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Phoenician city of Tyre was famous for making Tyrian purple dye from sea snails.

parts.note: steps read as dance steps, not measures taken by an authority

explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed in some cultures to summon rainfall when the land is parched.

clue.text: A Tory fixed seal with lugs

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician repaired a seal that had handles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges A TORY; 'lugs' is slang for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: An otary is an eared seal, such as a sea lion, with visible external ears unlike true seals.

clue.text: List not used at the cheese counter

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopping list is ignored while buying from the deli cheese section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges LIST NOT; the definition describes a product found at a cheese counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue cheese, one of the staples sold over a cheese counter.

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out loud, so the clue words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: about gives RE, as in regarding, and James is the Irish novelist James Joyce

explanation.surface: Someone is happy about a declaration made by James.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) plus JOYCE (the novelist James), spoken, sounds like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great happiness, the same as being glad.

indicators.note: unfinished says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ... is British slang for pudding, the course eaten ... the main meal

explanation.surface: A dessert was left half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' takes the last S off AFTERS; 'left' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: After and behind both mean following later in place or time.

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters spin round into a new order

explanation.surface: A vessel comes about to sail clear of an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges SHIP CLEAR; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, which is round in every direction.

clue.text: She's reported to be in form

definitions.text: She's reported to be in form

parts.words: She's reported to be in form
parts.note: in form means in a school class, and reported refers to school reports

explanation.definitionFit: A girl pupil belongs to a class, which British schools call a form, and gets termly school reports.

definitions.meaning: a heart-throb is a man women find irresistible, a seducer
read literally, someone who stops hearts is a female killer

explanation.definitionFit: A womanizing charmer is a heart-throb, and read literally the phrase names a female murderer.

parts.note: square in the sense of honest and direct means straight
on, as in moving on, means forward

explanation.surface: Continuing the boat picture: facing squarely ahead, it is plain sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's ship but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightforward task is simple and uncomplicated, which is what easy means.
The verb sense is to arouse interest, and the noun sense is a secret scheming plot.

parts.note: a Brownie is a classic Kodak box camera, not a junior Girl Guide; its eye is the lens opening

explanation.definitionFit: The opening that admits light in a camera acts as its eye, letting the image in.

definitions.meaning: an archaic german is a close relative, as in cousin-german, so germans are kin
affairs, as in dealings or love affairs

explanation.definitionFit: Relatives are germans in the old sense, and dealings or liaisons between people are affairs.

indicators.note: awkward signals that the letters are clumsily jumbled
extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: This clumsy clue is not very clever at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' turns CLUE into LUCE; 'extremely' takes NT, the ends of NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucent means shining or giving off light, a literary synonym for bright.
Bleak weather is cold and exposed, and the bleak is also a small European river fish.

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone off and been spoiled into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's given name.

definitions.meaning: a raised wooden flooring, as in a garden

explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn, as with garlands, and timber garden flooring is also called by this word.

indicators.note: of says the author's name is taken from within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asks who wrote the 1940s film noir about a blue flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Dahlia was actually written by Raymond Chandler; the name sits at the start of 'Dahlia'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British writer of children's books and macabre short stories.

clue.text: Halfway through, Emma made trial of marriage

indicators.note: halfway through points to the latter half of the word
made in the sense of fashioned into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Midway through, Emma tried out living as a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfway through' takes MA, the second half of EMMA; 'made' rearranges TRIAL into RITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective for things relating to marriage or to husband and wife.

clue.text: One of the Spices came out

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of the Spice Girls made a public announcement about herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CAME; the surface suggests the pop group and coming out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from the dried lacy covering of the nutmeg seed.

clue.text: An Indian contribution to British industry

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Indian person makes a contribution to the British economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the last letter of 'British' and the start of 'industry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, the majority religion of India.

parts.note: in racing a maiden is a horse that has never won a race

explanation.definitionFit: A maiden in horse racing is a runner yet to win, so by definition has only ever lost.
